"Unto Hashem Your God": Up to the Throne of Glory, and "Ashur Will Not Save Us"

p: "Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God"
for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory."
that the teshuvah itself reaches up to the Throne of Glory.
up to the Throne of Glory.
are found also in the Pesikta
אֶלָּא עַד מַהֲלַךְ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנִים
but a distance of five hundred years' journey;
and not only to the first firmament, etc.,
דָּבָר אַחֵר, עַד ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
Another interpretation: "unto Hashem your God," etc.
"For my iniquities have passed over my head,"
כִּי עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ רַבּוּ עַד לְמַעְלָה רֹאשׁ וְגוֹ׳
"For our iniquities have multiplied up above our head," etc.
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them:
if they reach up to the firmament
and not only up to the first, etc.,
but even up to the seventh,
up to the Throne of Glory.
This is as we have said
and this is why he expounded
and this follows the first explanation,
that the teshuvah reaches up to the Throne of Glory.
as referring to the magnitude of the sins:
"For my iniquities have passed over my head"
and "our iniquities have multiplied up above our head."
that is, that the sin was
up to the aspect of Kesser;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל הַכֹּל מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה.
And this is at the third meal,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him
that is, that the name Yisrael
then Avraham too was called Yisrael,
and likewise Yitzchak was called Yisrael,
there was still dross in them,
as Avraham Avinu set store by Yishmael
and said, "If only Yishmael might live before You"
But after the birth of Yaakov,
when his name was called Yisrael,
that they are not included in the seed of Avraham and Yitzchak,
And the essence of Yaakov's middah
from my beginning until this day"
And this is what the navi said
we will not ride upon horses," etc.
as they said in the Gemara
"When I pay reward to Avraham, etc.,
who ran before Me like horses";
is always to be engaged in activity.
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose middah was love of Hashem,
of the positive mitzvos of "arise and do,"
but was always in effort and alacrity,
as they said in the Gemara
that Hashem Yisbarach said to him,
But Yaakov Avinu said of himself,
from my beginning until this day,"
meaning that even all his effort
and he has nothing at all of his own;
and this is the main thing.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is what David HaMelech, peace be upon him, said
"Not in the strength of the horse does He delight,
nor does He favor the legs of a man," etc.
that Hashem Yisbarach's desire is not
in the strength of the horse?
and it corresponds to engaging in avodah
and he says that this is not yet
And "nor the legs of a man"
means the strength of a man,
and this corresponds to engaging in fear of Heaven,
for he is the mighty one who conquers his yetzer;
in this too "He does not favor,"
for this is not yet the full perfection;
rather, "Hashem favors those who fear Him,
those who hope for His kindness"
And this is the middah of Yaakov,
who said that he has nothing from his own side,
and bestows upon him from His kindness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר עֶזְרִי מֵעִם ה׳ וְגוֹ׳,
as he said, "My help is from Hashem," etc.,
And in truth Avraham and Yitzchak too
that after the birth of Yaakov
that there was still dross in their seed,
that even all of his effort
from the power of Hashem Yisbarach,
כִּי גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ,
"For also all our deeds You have wrought for us,"
then of itself it becomes clear
עָשׂוּ מַה נֶּגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
they did something against the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
that from the very beginning of Creation
Hashem Yisbarach foresaw in His deeds
and that it would be like the creation of the world:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּלֵּי,
except that which comes forth from within darkness, etc.;
and that from everything there will be "very good,"
that willful sins will be made into merits.
And this is the meaning of "up to the Throne of Glory":
that it becomes clarified in all ten sefiros,
And this is "Ashur will not save us":
is named for power and might,
שֶׁכָּל הָאוּמּוֹת נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם אַשּׁוּר
that all the nations were called by the name Ashur
because they make themselves mighty, etc.;
and their power is in deed and might,
"I said: It is but empty talk;
counsel and might are for war";
וְזֶה כְּנֶגֶד לֹא בְשׁוֹקֵי הָאִישׁ יִרְצֶה.
and this corresponds to "nor does He favor the legs of a man."
meaning that we will not trust
which is termed "the strength of the horse,"
'our god' to the work of our hands":
that is, regarding the deed in the service of Hashem,
we will not say "our god" to the work of our hands,
attributing it to our own strength,
but rather "the God Who shepherds me,"
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach.
"For in You the orphan finds compassion"
one who has no help at all from his own side,
only "my help," from the mercy of Heaven.
And when we recognize this in truth,
and He says, "Everything was from Me,
"I will heal their waywardness; I will love them freely":
that there shines forth in the heart
"I will be like the dew to Israel," etc.,
that the deeds that were not good
will also give off a good fragrance,
as we said (in the previous maamar).
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach,
and then we merit complete teshuvah,
so that from everything there will be merits.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a — "Rabbi Levi said: Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

rich.text: Yoma 86a

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 12 — “As explained in the Reishis Chochmah on what they said (Yoma 86a), ‘Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,’ meaning that it is effective even for a sin that reached up to the Throne of Glory. And in truth both explanations are in the Pesikta (Shuvah)… ‘even up to the Throne of Glory, and you do teshuvah, I accept you at once.’” Connection: Both weigh the two readings of “teshuvah reaches up to the Throne of Glory.”

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 44 — "Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded: Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, immediately it rises — not ten mil, not twenty, not a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; and not to the first firmament but to the seventh; and not only to the seventh, but it stands before the Throne of Glory. So Hoshea says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

paragraphs.text: Chullin 16a — “Rabbi was teaching: From where do we know that slaughter must be with a detached object? For it is said, He took the knife to slaughter. ... But that verse teaches us Avraham's eagerness.” The Gemara questions whether taking the knife proves a rule about slaughtering implements or simply displays Avraham's eagerness to fulfill the command.

p: And the portion of Shuvah concludes
"Whoever is wise, let him understand these things;
whoever is discerning, let him know them;
for the ways of Hashem are straight,
and the righteous walk in them," etc.
The matter is based on what is said
and a fool cannot understand this."
מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כְּלוּם יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם,
who has no fear of Heaven at all,
so that the words of Torah
have not yet entered the heart
and they teach him nothing at all;
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool
to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?"
עַל מִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
about one who has no fear of Heaven,
who has no heart at all.
something as plain as if visible to the eye,
which refers to the Holy One, blessed be He,
meaning that He stands before one's eyes;
so too the Shechinah is called "zos,"
as they said in the holy Zohar
as though it were plainly visible to the eye,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רל, א)
"He is Truth and She is Faith."
For there are two aspects of fear:
enter into the words of Torah at all,
and this is called "the outer keys"
as they said in the holy Zohar
the essence and root of all worlds," etc.;
and it is the aspect of "Binah is the heart"
which enters the depths of the heart,
and the Torah is the gateway to it
"May He open our heart to His Torah,"
that the words of Torah should enter the heart,
"and place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him";
"What does Hashem your God ask of you,
from Hashem Yisbarach as a gift,
as is brought in the name of
הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בֶּער זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
the Rebbe, Reb Ber, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
the allusion: "It is the way of a man
But when the love comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
אָז בָּא גַּם הַיִּרְאָה עִלָּאָה כְּאֶחָד,
then the higher fear comes along with it,
as they said in the holy Zohar
that is, even what is plain before the eye,
who has a heart to understand
he will not grasp, in the aspect of Daas,
And likewise here it says "Whoever is wise,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים אֵינוֹ כְּסִיל,
meaning that at least he is not a fool,
what is plain before the eye,
like the aspect of "zos," as mentioned above.
"Whoever is discerning, let him know them":
one is "discerning" when the fear enters
into the depths of the heart,
in the manner of what is said (Mishlei 2:5),
"Then you will understand the fear of Hashem";
and this is the higher fear;
such a one can attain the middah of Daas,
which is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon;
אָז יָבִין כִּי יְשָׁרִים דַּרְכֵי ה׳,
then he will understand that "the ways of Hashem are straight,"
Regarding "to declare," it is stated in the holy Zohar
that it is "the secret of wisdom,"
which is the joining of Chochmah and Binah:
that in truth "the tzaddik will flourish like a palm"
And this is what it says, "the righteous walk in them":
that one who is truly of the seed of Israel
does not fall on account of
seeing the tranquility of the wicked
and the lowliness of Israel in this world.
Only one who is not of the seed of Yaakov,
when he sees the tranquility of the wicked in this world,
as Rashi, of blessed memory, wrote
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בָּהֶן אֶחָד
that it is impossible that there not be among them one
inclines his heart to avodah zarah;
and this is "but transgressors stumble in them."
This is not so for one who is
truly of the seed of Yaakov:
and they see that "the ways of Hashem are straight":
that in truth the tzaddik will flourish like a palm in the future,
while the tranquility of the wicked
is only so that they be destroyed forever.
"Fortunate is the man who does this (zos)"
that everything be plainly visible to the eye,
and we attain a semblance of the World to Come.
Therefore this psalm was established for Shabbos,
which is a semblance of the World to Come,
And were Israel to keep Shabbos properly,
they would immediately be redeemed completely
וְאָז יְבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח גַּם כֵּן,
and then death too would be swallowed up forever,
as they said in the Yerushalmi
"He will swallow up death forever," etc.,
and his time has come to be swallowed up;
But the world is judged by its majority,
if it keeps Shabbos according to its halachah,
and death will be swallowed up.
his death is not called death,
but rather like sleep and awakening.
And accordingly, on Shabbos one can
so that willful sins become like merits,
since one attains fear and love in completeness
and merits the aspect of Daas,
and therefore the portion of Shuvah concludes with this.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b, s.v. Kedei learbev — “The Aruch explains, as in the Yerushalmi: It is written, He shall swallow death forever, and On that day a great shofar shall be sounded. When he hears the shofar once, he is alarmed but not fully alarmed. When he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the shofar that shall be sounded as the great shofar, and my time has come to be swallowed up. He becomes confused and has no time to prosecute.” This verifies the teaching through Tosafos quoting the Aruch in the Yerushalmi's name, the intermediary identified in Rav Tzadok's citation. It is not presented as an independently located passage in the extant Yerushalmi.
